Potential notable citations

About this page, and how a candidate is read
This page is for the applicant’s review, not for counsel. packet.html holds only the citations confirmed for the filing; nothing on this page is in it. Tick a row, or send the row_uids, and the pipeline (discover-pdfs.js → file-pdf.js → scan-mentions.js → record-evidence.js) reads the full text, finds the section and page, and files it at the tier the text supports. Where a PDF is already on file, the Tier and Citation columns carry what that reading found; where it is not, they say so and claim nothing.

How the list was derived: the screen for each cited work

439 of the 754 citations have a PDF on file and have been read by the scanner; those carry a tier and the sentence it rests on. The rest have no tier because nothing has been read, which is a statement about the file, not about the paper.

754 independent citations of these works are not in the packet and were not used in the original application. Each is a real, independently authored citation. They appear as 669 rows below, because 55 articles cite more than one of my works and is shown once, with a separate tier and quotation for each work it cites. 409 citations have been read and the sentence that cites the tool is recorded; 30 have been read and the tool does not appear anywhere the article ranks as a section; 315 have no PDF yet, so where the citation sits is still unknown — and that is what decides a tier.

The screen below counts citations, not articles: independence and tier are both judgements about one citing paper against one cited work, so a paper that cites two of my works is screened twice and decides twice. The table then folds those onto one row.

Notes on the list, and how the table is read

Filtering is screen only: a printed or PDF copy of this page always shows every candidate, so what is on screen cannot silently decide what gets filed.

One row is one citing article; the “My work” column says which of my papers it cites. 754 citations appear as 669 rows. An article that cites two of my works is one row with two blocks in the “My work”, Tier and Citation columns, and each block is judged on its own: a tier for GLAD in that article says nothing about where GlycoGlyph sits in it, and one work can be filed while the other is not. The row leads with every row_uid it carries, because the uid — not the title — is the handle the pipeline takes.

“Open copy” is a statement about access, not about the paper. Open copy found means a downloadable version exists and, where the PDF column has a link, it is already in this folder. Paywalled means the article is real and the publisher gates the file — an access the applicant’s own subscription or an interlibrary loan can settle. No open copy and Not in OpenAlex mean the look-up completed and found nothing downloadable; they are not findings that the paper does not exist, and a publisher page or a library copy can still supply the text.

Independence was re-checked against the citation record, not the queued snapshot. The record reads the complete author list of both papers. A citing paper that shares an author with the cited work, or that names Richard D. Cummings or the former PI Umesh R. Desai, is a self-citation and was removed at the first screen above.

A tier is a scan result, and only for an article that has actually been read. The Tier and Citation columns are filled from the PDF on file: scan-mentions.js extracts the text, finds every appearance of the tool, and reads the heading the article itself printed above it. Tier A means the mention sits in the Methods as the method performed; B in the Results or Figures; C in a high-reputation publication; D an acknowledgement. Where the column says no tier, the article was read and the tool appears only in a reference list, a table, or a section that earns no tier — the note says which. Where it says not read, no PDF exists yet, so no claim is made. A scan is a machine reading of prose: it is good at telling a Methods sentence from a bibliography entry, and it cannot tell whether the use was substantial. A person’s reading of the page decides, and filing a candidate runs the same scanner again into the packet.

A blue “Tier X — resolved” pill means the citing paper never names the tool. A citing author who used the work often credits it only as a reference number (“following established procedures [125–127]”, a superscript 69) or, in author–year journals, only as “(Mehta et al. 2024)”. scan-refs.js identifies which bibliography entry is the applicant’s paper — two signals required, title plus year plus first author, never a guess — and then reports every place that number or that citation is credited, with the section and the sentence. The tier bar is identical to a named mention’s: under a heading the citing paper printed, in prose, not a table cell and not the reference list. The colour only says how the citation was found, not that it is weaker.

How a candidate becomes part of the packet

This page is read-only, deliberately. There is no checkbox and no button, because a tick on a screen belongs to nobody: it is lost on reload, it cannot be inspected by anyone else, and nothing downstream could tell whether you meant it. A decision is recorded in notable-citations.sqlite instead, and the way to make one is to tell the assistant the row_uid you want filed. It then runs scripts/record-evidence.js, which refuses unless you give it a sentence quoted verbatim from the citing article and it can find that exact sentence in the PDF on file — so a filed quotation is checked against the document rather than written from memory. The row’s status becomes included, its folder moves into papers/, and packet.html is re-rendered so the entry and its detail section appear together. A row decided against is screened-out with the reason recorded, and stays in screened-out.csv so it is not reconsidered from scratch later.

What the page is for, then, is the reading: filter to a work or a tier, open the PDF from the “PDF on file” column, judge the sentence, and quote it back.

Citation reports

Each row_uid and each citing-paper title links to that article’s report in citation-report.html, which opens on the uid (?uid=cit-000544). The report shows the article once, with its authors, senior author, open copy and files, and then every citation of my work the article holds, with the one you opened highlighted. Each citation section gives the work it cites, where the citation sits, and the quotation. A report is a review note, not evidence: nothing in it reaches counsel unless the row is confirmed and the packet is re-rendered.
